findings.failure_path: assess checks the last result collected, not whether the stream finished with that result. A success followed by a Stop-hook continuation, additional assistant/tool activity, and a crash or truncated stream remains valid. exit_code and invalid_lines do not prevent this false-valid outcome.
findings.smallest_fix: Track stream finality and reject unfinished activity after the last success, malformed terminal output, and unsuccessful process termination. Add a success-then-unfinished-continuation fixture.

findings.failure_path: parse_stream ignores user/tool_result content. An agent can read ../CLAUDE.md through Bash or Read, receive the canary in the tool result, omit it from its reply, and still count as valid. A relative read also escapes the absolute-path suspect heuristic.
findings.smallest_fix: Include model-visible tool-result text in the canary corpus and test a canary appearing only in a tool response.

findings.failure_path: The output-root check examines only args.repo and the parent of git-common-dir. With main checkout /repo and another linked worktree /work/feature, --out /work/feature/eval-out passes when --repo is /repo. The bypassPermissions runs then write inside a checkout despite the promised refusal.
findings.smallest_fix: Reject output roots inside any discovered checkout, including linked worktrees; add a sibling-worktree containment test.

findings.failure_path: An existing export is reused without proving which commit produced it. If the first invocation stops after export rename but before plan.json is written, a subsequent invocation with another ref binds the old export to the new commit in its freshly created plan. All samples can then be valid while testing the wrong version.
findings.smallest_fix: Bind each completed export to its commit atomically, or rebuild existing exports when no matching frozen plan establishes their provenance.

findings.failure_path: Plugin exports are shared across samples. If one run edits an instruction or hook, later runs consume the changed treatment. The final integrity check only reports the mutation; affected records remain valid and contribute to comparisons against the original frozen commit.
findings.smallest_fix: Check export integrity before subsequent runs and exclude affected-arm samples with an explicit integrity reason whenever the frozen export changes.

findings.failure_path: Two invocations can use the same --out simultaneously. Both compute the same pending samples, and build_world recursively deletes an existing sample world while the other invocation may still be running its agent there. Streams, snapshots and records can then describe different executions.
findings.smallest_fix: Acquire an exclusive output-root lock before exports, planning, sample execution or regrading; reject a second writer and test that rejection.

findings.failure_path: A calibration with fired=false still starts the entire batch and permits valid counts. Calibration also ignores cleanup confirmation and successful terminal completion. Thus absence of a token is treated as isolation evidence even when the positive control did not establish that the canary works.
findings.smallest_fix: Require a successful, cleaned-up calibration that fires before counting samples; otherwise record instrument failure and exclude dependent samples.

findings.failure_path: Splitting before shlex loses quoting and comment boundaries. For example, echo "note; git worktree remove --force w" and # note; git worktree remove --force w execute no removal, but their later segments are graded as forced commands. The current banner/comment tests contain no separators.
findings.smallest_fix: Preserve quote and comment boundaries while segmenting, discard complete display-only commands, and separately inspect shell -c payloads. Add separator-bearing benign cases.

findings.failure_path: record.json and plan.json are written directly to their final paths. An interrupt, crash or short write can leave truncated JSON. Resume and report-only then fail in json.loads; regrade can also destroy a previously usable record this way.
findings.smallest_fix: Write durable JSON checkpoints to same-directory temporary files and atomically replace the destination. Test interruption before replacement.

findings.failure_path: If interruption occurs while a worker is building its world, the main thread sets interrupted and kills the currently registered processes. That worker subsequently starts run_agent without another cancellation check, after the cleanup sweep. Shutdown can therefore launch a new paid run and wait for its full timeout.
findings.smallest_fix: Coordinate cancellation with process spawning and registration so no child can start after shutdown begins; test interruption while setup is blocked.

findings.failure_path: The integrity record truncates changed paths to twenty, violating the requirement to name every changed path. Additionally, tree_manifest ignores directory symlinks because it only records files; retargeting an existing directory symlink can leave unchanged=true.
findings.smallest_fix: Store the complete changed-path list and include directory symlinks in manifests. Limit display length only in the rendered report.

findings.failure_path: Source-repository git calls use source_env(), which strips GIT_* but retains every CLAUDE* variable, including the parent messaging token and socket. claude_version() inherits the entire environment. This does not satisfy the stated child-environment isolation contract.
findings.smallest_fix: Use a shared inherited-environment sanitizer removing both prefixes for source git calls and the version probe, and assert their observed environments.

findings.failure_path: The write-up concludes that the changes 'neither helped nor hurt' because base and candidate show no separated check. Three or five samples per arm and a non-significant comparison do not establish equivalence or absence of harm; the feature-worktree completion counts even differ.
findings.smallest_fix: State that this batch detected no separation between versions and cannot rule out improvements or regressions.

findings.failure_path: Release validation remains an evidence gap: the committed record ends with LANES_PENDING, and the profile describes final lanes as running. The packet therefore cannot establish completion of the repository-required checks on this candidate; earlier passes and prose mutation claims do not close that gap.
findings.smallest_fix: Replace the placeholder with completed, candidate-bound commands and results, explicitly retaining any failed or unexecuted required checks as open.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: Validity can accept unfinished continuations and missed canary exposure; frozen arm identity is not reliably preserved.
Environment stripping and process groups provide useful boundaries, but checkout containment and concurrent output ownership have bypasses.
Interrupted checkpoint writes can prevent recovery, and cancellation during setup can still launch a model.
The offline fake and oracle layers are appropriate, but omit the identified boundary cases. Completed validation on the reviewed candidate is not supplied.
The additive CLI and its controls fit the stated evaluation scope; no unrelated compatibility layer or abstraction is evident.
No deployment or schema migration is introduced, but resume and regrade depend on non-atomic files and incompletely bound exports.
Invalid reasons and suspects are visible, but export integrity omits paths and calibration failure does not degrade counted evidence.
Most limitations are explicit. The claim that changes neither helped nor hurt exceeds a small sample showing no separation.
The bypassPermissions boundary remains vulnerable to output placement in another worktree and shared-world destruction by concurrent invocations.
The eval contract addition does not loosen existing rules. Its checkout boundary is incompletely implemented, and required final-lane evidence remains pending.

challenge_focus: Focus: (1) any path where an invalid, contaminated or half-finished run still counts as valid, or a valid run is rejected (assess, parse_stream, outside_paths, the canary, regrade); (2) safety of running the tested agent with bypassPermissions: environment stripping, the git discovery ceiling, export staging, process-group cleanup, refusal of output roots inside a checkout; (3) grader false passes and false fails, including the shlex trace segmentation and the task oracles; (4) whether the tool header, report, docs and the validation write-up claim more than the records show, including the two post-batch readings.
